# Cross-correlation function (CCF) plot for two time series

## Description

Plots the correlation between one time series and lagged versions of another across a range of lags.

```r
plot_crosscorrelation(
  data,
  var,
  time,
  type = c("cov", "cov"),
  method = "pearson",
  lags = 0:9,
  pop = NULL,
  unit = NULL,
  aggregate_space = NULL,
  aggregate_space_fun = "mean",
  facet = FALSE,
  title = NULL,
  var_label = NULL,
  legend = NULL,
  ylab = NULL,
  xlab = NULL,
  palette = NULL,
  area = NULL
)
```

## Arguments

- `data`: Data frame containing equally spaced (daily, weekly, monthly) covariate or disease case observations for one or multiple locations.
- `var`: A character vector of length 2 identifying the variables to be included. The second variable is the one that is lagged.
- `time`: Name of the variable that identifies the temporal dimension of the data frame. Its values must be in date format ("yyyy-mm-dd") representing the day of observation for daily data, the first day of the week for weekly, or the first day of the month for monthly observations.
- `type`: A character vector of length 2 that specifies the types of variable in `var`. Possible values include 'cov' (covariate, default), 'counts' (case counts), and 'inc' (case incidence). If `type='inc'`, `pop` is required.
- `method`: Correlation method. Options include "pearson" (default), "spearman" or "kendall".
- `lags`: Numerical vector indicating the lags at which the cross-correlation should be computed. The second variable in 'var' will be lagged.
- `pop`: Character identifying the variable name for population. Only needed if `type='inc'`.
- `unit`: Name of the variable that identifies the different units for which a time series is available, typically a spatial unit.
- `aggregate_space`: Name of variable used to define spatial aggregation groups that contain the different units.
- `aggregate_space_fun`: Character indicating the function to be used in the aggregation over space for `type="cov"`. Options are "mean" (default), "median", "sum". For case counts and incidence, "sum" is always applied.
- `facet`: If TRUE a separate time series for each space unit is plotted in different facets.
- `title`: Optional title of the plot.
- `var_label`: A character vector of length 2 with custom names for 'var' (in the same order).
- `legend`: Character with a custom name for the legend.
- `ylab`: Label for the y-axis.
- `xlab`: Label for the x-axis.
- `palette`: GHR, RColorBrewer or colorspace palette. Use "-" before the palette name (e.g., "-Reds") to reverse it.
- `area`: Deprecated, use `unit` instead.

## Details

Correlations are computed after deleting missing rows in the lag data so that every correlation is computed with the same observations.

## Returns

A ggplot2 cross-correlation plot.

## Examples

```r
# Load data
data("dengue_MS")
data("dengue_SP")

# Cross-correlation (Pearson) between dengue counts and enso (single unit)
plot_crosscorrelation(
  data = dengue_SP,
  var = c("cases", "enso"),
  type = c("counts", "cov"),
  time = "date"
)

# Cross-correlation (Spearman) between dengue inc and tmax for multiple areas
plot_crosscorrelation(
  data = dengue_MS,
  var = c("dengue_cases", "tmax"),
  type = c("inc", "cov"),
  pop = "population",
  time = "date",
  unit = "micro_name",
  method = "spearman"
)

# Cross-correlation (Kendall) between dengue inc and pdsi for multiple areas
# aggregated by mesoregion, faceted, with custom labels
plot_crosscorrelation(
  data = dengue_MS,
  var = c("dengue_cases", "pdsi"),
  type = c("inc", "cov"),
  pop = "population",
  time = "date",
  unit = "micro_name",
  method = "kendall",
  aggregate_space = "meso_name",
  facet = TRUE,
  title = "Cross-correlation for meso areas"
)
```
